paragraphs.text: I see evidently by his deeds, that sin pushes forward the reprobate from wickedness to wickedness, even though he goes about to cover his impiety.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Though all others detest his vile sin, yet he himself sees it not.
paragraphs.label: b
paragraphs.anchor: flattereth himself in his own eyes

paragraphs.text: The reprobates mock wholesome doctrine, and put no difference between good and evil.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: By describing at large the nature of the reprobate, he admonishes the godly to beware of these vices.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Though wickedness seems to overflow all the world, yet by your heavenly providence you govern heaven and earth.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: The depth of your providence governs all things, and disposes them, even though the wicked seem to overwhelm the world.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Only God's children have enough of all things both concerning this life and the life to come.
paragraphs.label: g
paragraphs.anchor: satisfied with the fatness of thy

paragraphs.text: He shows who God's children are, that is, they who know him, and live their lives uprightly.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Let not the proud advance himself against me, or the power of the wicked drive me away.
paragraphs.label: i
paragraphs.anchor: foot of pride come against me

paragraphs.text: That is, in their pride in which they flatter themselves.
